messages:
nina: Quick update 1h canary of vectis13b (int4) on dedicated. Seeing steady mem-frag and two OOMs when bursts include long-context requests. Hoping to get quick triage suggestions.

omar: Can you paste the canary config and single-run perf numbers? avg seq len, p50/p99, and failure traces would help.

nina: Pasted config we used:
```
model: vectis13b-int4
batch_size: 12
max_new_tokens: 512
prefetch: 4
kv_prefetch: true
async_prefetch: true
microbatch_window: 0.25
soft_reserve: 0.10
```
Perf snapshot: avg seq=190, tail up to 1600. p50 85ms, p99 620ms. OOMs correlated with two concurrent long seqs + batch spikes.

felix: Hypothesis: int4 path increases tiny allocation count for KV/prefetch buffers and `async_prefetch` + larger `batch_size` causes freelist fragmentation. microbatch_window means we hold more per-request buffers concurrently.

sophia: Also callout: we saw subtle quality drift on long sequences in initial A/B (repetition + drop in avg log-likelihood) vs int8 baseline. Need to separate mem/latency fixes from quant quality fixes.

felix: Quick experiments to run (low-risk):
1) run-1: batch=6, async_prefetch=false, max_new_tokens=256
2) run-2: batch=12, async_prefetch=true, but enable kv_trim_interval=3s and slot_compactor.aggr=high
3) run-3: batch=8, disable microbatching (microbatch_window=0)

nina: Kicked off 3 runs. deploy job #9981 started for run-1.

deploy-bot: deployment job #9981 started: canary-vectis13b-int4 -> pool-dedicated-09.

nina: run-1 after 25m: stable, fragmentation plateaued ~52%, no OOMs. throughput -18% vs baseline. Latency p99 +10%.

nina: run-2 after 20m: we still saw one OOM at 18m but fragmentation growth much slower. slot_compactor helped but couldn't catch immediate spikes when two long sequences arrived together.

nina: run-3 after 22m: mixed results. Some microbursts still create holes, but overall better than baseline. No OOMs so far.

felix: Interpretation: combination of disabling async_prefetch and lowering batch gets us out of the OOM window. Aggressive compaction helps but is reactive and can't always keep up during simultaneous long requests.

sophia: For the quality regression: running eval harness (500 mixed-length prompts) comparing int4 vs int8. Early results: int4 avg token-level NLL delta +0.9, and we see a spike in token-repeat events on sequences >1024. Will continue to run full sweep.

omar: Ops asks: add these metrics to canary dashboards ASAP: `kv_alloc_rate`, `slab_fragmentation_ratio`, `freelist_hole_count`, `kv_eviction_count_per_min`. Set soft alert when `kv_eviction_count_per_min` > 20 or fragmentation_ratio > 0.75 for >5m. Also add fallback policy: auto-route new long-seq requests (>1024 tokens) to large-memory hosts.

nina: I'll open PR with per-model default proposal: {"batch_size":"8","max_new_tokens":"256","prefetch":"2","async_prefetch":"false","kv_trim_interval":"3s","slot_compactor.aggr":"high"} and the new alerts + fallback rule. Will include a short rollback policy and tag the perf run links.

felix: For rollout gating include a 500-run long-context regression: fail if NLL delta > 1.5 or repeat-rate increases > 1%. If quality fails, plan is to: 1) try int8 on dedicated, 2) try mixed-precision (kv int8, weights int4) if feasible, or 3) keep int4 but enforce stricter per-request caps and route long seqs.

sophia: I'll upload the eval diffs and a short sample of problematic generations to the PR so reviewers can see examples (token spans and exact prompts).

nina: Action items: nina PR with defaults/alerts/fallback; sophia full eval; felix add compactor patch and run a perf harness sweep for batch sizes {6,8,10}; omar wire metrics to canary dashboard.

deploy-bot: deployment job #9981 success: canary stable at 30m.

nina: Thanks team. We'll hold canary scaling until eval finishes. Will post PR link and artifacts here when ready. :rocket:
